pitch: Exploit high-bandwidth RAM across many Cloudflare Edge Workers: explode a dataset too large for one machine into per-worker memory, run SIMD/MIMD-style anomaly detection and incremental training across workers, and persist only the deltas -- so a model can be trained on data that would not fit in one machine's memory. Target: live in 30 days.

out_of_scope_v1.title: Multi-tenancy and auth
out_of_scope_v1.why: Nothing in the pitch names more than one user or dataset owner; adding access control before the architecture is even validated would be solving a problem that may not exist yet.

out_of_scope_v1.title: Autoscaling policy
out_of_scope_v1.why: Cloudflare already autoscales Workers; a custom policy is only worth designing once ops-e2e shows the default behaviour is actually a problem.

out_of_scope_v1.title: Detector quality tuning beyond baseline parity
out_of_scope_v1.why: kernel-accuracy asks 'does sharding cost accuracy', not 'is this the best possible detector' -- tuning belongs after the architecture is proven, not before.

out_of_scope_v1.title: Cold-start optimisation
out_of_scope_v1.why: A slower first request per worker is a UX problem, not an architecture problem; irrelevant until ops-e2e shows it matters at target scale.

nodes.title: Edge-RAM anomaly training pipeline
nodes.text: Exploit high-bandwidth RAM across many Cloudflare Edge Workers: explode a dataset too large for one machine into per-worker memory, run SIMD/MIMD-style anomaly detection and incremental training across workers, and persist only the deltas -- so a model can be trained on data that would not fit in one machine's memory. Target: live in 30 days.
nodes.covers_why: Root node; no single 'covers' judgement applies to the whole pitch.

nodes.title: Platform limits
nodes.text:
What Cloudflare's Workers platform actually gives you, measured or looked up, before anything else is sized against it.
Listed child items: Measure the per-isolate memory ceiling, Measure worker-to-worker transfer, Confirm WASM SIMD availability, Measure concurrency and fan-out ceilings, Measure exchange bandwidth and price.
nodes.covers_why: Memory ceiling, shared memory, SIMD availability, fan-out and exchange cost are the five concrete platform facts the rest of the architecture depends on.

nodes.title: Ingest and sharding
nodes.text:
Getting the source dataset in and split into per-worker chunks that fit inside the platform's real limits.
Listed child items: Choose where the source dataset lives, Size the per-worker chunk, Build the shard loader.
nodes.covers_why: Source, chunk size and the loader that builds on them fully cover getting data from source to worker.

nodes.title: Per-worker compute
nodes.text:
The anomaly-detection kernel that runs inside one worker's own memory, and whether sharded detection is even accurate enough to ship.
Listed child items: Choose a streaming-friendly anomaly algorithm, Measure the per-invocation compute budget, Build and benchmark the SIMD kernel, Validate accuracy against a single-machine baseline.
nodes.covers_why: Algorithm choice, implementation and an accuracy check against a real baseline cover picking, building and validating the kernel.

nodes.title: Cross-worker exchange
nodes.text:
Coordinating many independent workers and moving only the anomalous deltas between them, since there is no shared memory to pass full results through.
Listed child items: Choose the coordination primitive, Define the delta format, Define the reduce step, Build dispatch and collect.
nodes.covers_why: Coordination primitive, delta format, reduce step and the implementation that builds them cover moving deltas between workers.

nodes.title: Model state and training
nodes.text:
Accumulating a trained model from a stream of deltas across many short-lived invocations, and persisting the running state between them.
Listed child items: Choose where accumulating state lives, Confirm the model supports incremental updates, Build state accumulation and reload.
nodes.covers_why: Where state lives and whether the model updates incrementally are two real questions, but neither addresses what happens when several workers finish at the same moment and all try to write the accumulated state. Last-write-wins silently loses updates; a single serialising writer becomes a bottleneck for a design whose whole premise is many workers training at once. That is a real hole, and nothing else in this plan fills it.

nodes.title: Correctness, operations and launch
nodes.text:
What a working prototype still needs before it can run unattended: failure handling, observability, a real cost figure, and a launch path. Missing from the pitch as given.
Listed child items: Handle worker failure, Add per-pass observability, Build a real cost projection, Run end-to-end at target scale, Deploy and launch.
nodes.covers_why: Failure handling, observability, a real cost figure and a launch path cover what a prototype needs before it can run unattended.

nodes.title: Measure the per-isolate memory ceiling
nodes.text: Deploy a Worker that allocates memory until the platform kills it, on this account's real plan tier, and record the ceiling.
nodes.duration_basis: Optimistic: the kill signal is unambiguous and the ceiling is read off in one run. Pessimistic: the kill is a CPU-time limit, not a memory limit, and the measurement has to be redesigned to isolate the real cause.
nodes.exit_criteria: A measured MB figure for this account's plan tier, not a documentation guess.
nodes.risk_reason: Every downstream chunk-size decision is sized against this number; if it's much smaller than assumed, ingest has to change shape.

nodes.title: Measure worker-to-worker transfer
nodes.text: Try to move a block of data from one Worker invocation to another without a network-facing API, and measure whatever bandwidth is actually achieved -- or confirm no such path exists.
nodes.duration_basis: Optimistic: the docs already settle it -- no shared-memory primitive exists, confirmed and done. Pessimistic: this is the pitch's central claim, so it's worth trying several near-misses (SharedArrayBuffer, a KV race, a Durable Object as a mailbox) before writing down a confident 'no'.
nodes.exit_criteria: Either a measured non-network transfer path with its bandwidth, or a documented confirmation none exists.

target_metric.name: worker-to-worker bandwidth off the network path
target_metric.assumed_today: very likely none exists (isolates are memory-isolated)

nodes.risk_reason: This is the pitch's central claim. If it's false as literally stated, the architecture is sharded-plus-network-exchange, not shared memory, and everything below is re-scoped, not merely delayed.

nodes.title: Confirm WASM SIMD availability
nodes.text: Confirm the Workers runtime's WebAssembly engine supports the SIMD instruction proposal, and get a rough sense of realistic speedup for a numeric anomaly-detection kernel.
nodes.duration_basis: Low-stakes docs lookup either way; the only slippage risk is the docs being unclear about which runtime version ships the proposal.
nodes.exit_criteria: Confirmed from current Cloudflare docs, with the speedup ballpark noted.
nodes.risk_reason: Low stakes and answerable by reading docs -- this part of the pitch is real.

nodes.title: Measure concurrency and fan-out ceilings
nodes.text: Measure the maximum simultaneous invocations and subrequests one deployment can sustain on this account's plan tier.
nodes.duration_basis: Pessimistic: the real ceiling is plan-tier-dependent and undocumented for the exact combination needed, so it may take a support ticket rather than a self-serve measurement.
nodes.exit_criteria: A measured concurrent-invocation ceiling and subrequest limit for this account.

target_metric.name: concurrent invocations x subrequests
target_metric.needed: ceiling x per-worker chunk >= dataset size

nodes.risk_reason: A generous per-isolate memory cap is worthless if only a handful of workers can run at once -- this is a platform limit, not an ingest design choice, which is why it moved here.

nodes.title: Measure exchange bandwidth and price
nodes.text: Measure achievable bytes/second and requests/second between a Worker and R2, and between a Worker and a Durable Object -- the channel every cross-worker exchange now has to use.
nodes.duration_basis: Two separate channels to benchmark (R2, Durable Objects), each with its own time-of-day variance; pessimistic case is re-running both to get a stable figure.
nodes.exit_criteria: Measured MB/s and requests/s for both paths, plus their per-unit price.

target_metric.name: Worker<->R2/Durable Object throughput
target_metric.needed: enough to move the delta stream within the pass-time budget
target_metric.assumed_today: R2 has no egress fee to Workers (documented); throughput unmeasured

nodes.risk_reason: This is the replacement for shared memory. It doesn't kill the idea the way spike-sharedmem coming back negative would, but it sizes whether the re-scoped design can hit its own pass-time target.

nodes.title: Choose where the source dataset lives
nodes.text: Choose where the large source dataset is actually read from -- Cloudflare R2, an external object store, or a streamed feed.
nodes.duration_basis: Optimistic: a same-day call once the trade-off is laid out. Pessimistic: this needs the user's calendar, not more analysis -- decision tasks slip on availability, not difficulty.
nodes.exit_criteria: One source chosen and reachable from a Worker.
nodes.risk_reason: A real cost/latency trade-off (R2 has no egress fee to Workers; external storage may) that only the user can settle.

nodes.title: Size the per-worker chunk
nodes.text: Decide chunk size once the real per-isolate memory ceiling and per-invocation time budget are both known, leaving headroom for the running process.
nodes.duration_basis: Only decidable once both upstream measurements land cleanly; if either was ambiguous this negotiation drags while a second measurement is sought.
nodes.exit_criteria: A chunk-size figure with its headroom margin stated.
nodes.risk_reason: Made responsibly only once both ceilings it depends on are measured, not guessed.

nodes.title: Build the shard loader
nodes.text: Build the loader that reads one chunk into a Worker's own memory, inside both the measured memory ceiling and the measured time budget.
nodes.duration_basis: First real implementation on the critical path; typical first-integration slip once the measured ceilings turn out tighter in practice than in a spike.
nodes.exit_criteria: Loads a chunk end-to-end within both measured ceilings, for every chunk in a real dataset.
nodes.risk_reason: First real implementation on the critical path; blocked entirely on the two measurements above landing first.

nodes.title: Choose a streaming-friendly anomaly algorithm
nodes.text: Choose an anomaly-detection method that can run one chunk at a time with no view of the whole dataset, since no single worker ever sees more than its own shard.
nodes.duration_basis: Same calendar risk as any decision task, compounded by a real technical trade-off (streaming z-score/IQR vs. online isolation-forest vs. sketch-based) that has to actually be presented, not just asked.
nodes.exit_criteria: One algorithm chosen with a stated reason it supports online/incremental scoring.
nodes.risk_reason: A real design choice (streaming z-score/IQR variants, an online isolation-forest variant, a sketch-based method) with accuracy trade-offs the plan alone can't resolve.

nodes.title: Measure the per-invocation compute budget
nodes.text: Run a realistic chunk of the chosen algorithm's computation inside a real Worker invocation and measure wall-clock time against the platform's per-invocation limit.
nodes.duration_basis: A representative chunk is hard to pick before the real loader exists; the pessimistic case is faking one, getting an unrepresentative number, and having to redo it once ingest-loader lands.
nodes.exit_criteria: Measured wall-clock time for a representative chunk, compared against the platform's hard per-invocation limit.

target_metric.name: compute time per chunk vs per-invocation CPU limit
target_metric.assumed_today: a hard per-invocation limit exists, plan-tier dependent

nodes.risk_reason: If a chunk's workload doesn't fit one invocation, the plan needs smaller chunks or a multi-invocation pattern -- worth knowing in week 1, not week 3.

nodes.title: Build and benchmark the SIMD kernel
nodes.text: Build the chosen anomaly-detection kernel in WASM with SIMD, and benchmark it against a plain (non-SIMD) version to confirm the speedup is real for this workload.
nodes.duration_basis: The single most novel, highest-skill-risk build in the plan -- WASM SIMD tuning has a long, unpredictable tail even for an experienced engineer.
nodes.exit_criteria: Kernel measurably faster than a scalar baseline on a representative chunk, within the measured time budget.
nodes.risk_reason: Only worth doing once the algorithm choice and the time-budget spike both say this is viable.

nodes.title: Validate accuracy against a single-machine baseline
nodes.text: Compare sharded, per-chunk online detection against a whole-dataset detector on the same data: does splitting the data cost real detection accuracy?
nodes.duration_basis: An unfavorable accuracy gap sends this back to kernel-algo for a second pass, not just a longer benchmark run -- the pessimistic case is one round-trip through that loop.
nodes.exit_criteria: A measured accuracy gap (or lack of one) between sharded and whole-dataset detection, against a stated tolerance.
nodes.risk_reason: The architecture can work perfectly and still be pointless if sharding costs too much detection accuracy. Nothing else in this plan asks this question.

nodes.title: Choose the coordination primitive
nodes.text: Pick how workers get coordinated and how work gets handed out: Durable Objects for stateful coordination, Queues for work distribution, or an external orchestrator outside Cloudflare.
nodes.duration_basis: A real architecture decision with cost/latency trade-offs; same calendar risk as other decision tasks.
nodes.exit_criteria: One primitive chosen with its cost/latency trade-off stated.
nodes.risk_reason: A real architecture decision with cost and latency trade-offs the plan can't make unilaterally.

nodes.title: Define the delta format
nodes.text: Define what each worker emits when it finds an anomaly -- small enough to move cheaply over the network, since that is now the only channel between workers.
nodes.duration_basis: A narrower decision than most here (format follows from the primitive already chosen), so the tail is shorter.
nodes.exit_criteria: A delta schema with a stated size budget per record.
nodes.risk_reason: Depends on which coordination primitive is chosen; a format cheap on Queues may be expensive on Durable Objects.

nodes.title: Define the reduce step
nodes.text: Define how deltas from many independent workers get merged into one picture -- deduplicated, ordered, or aggregated as appropriate.
nodes.duration_basis: Ordering/dedupe guarantees are subtle and easy to under-scope on a first pass; pessimistic case is a second design pass once a gap is noticed.
nodes.exit_criteria: A reduce algorithm defined and its ordering/dedupe guarantees stated.
nodes.risk_reason: A design detail that follows once the delta format is fixed.

nodes.title: Build dispatch and collect
nodes.text: Build the actual dispatch of chunks to workers and collection of their deltas, across the chosen coordination primitive.
nodes.duration_basis: The first real exercise of the platform's true concurrency ceiling rather than an assumed one -- likely to surface surprises the fan-out spike didn't catch.
nodes.exit_criteria: Dispatches N workers and collects their deltas end-to-end, within the measured fan-out ceiling.
nodes.risk_reason: The first implementation that actually exercises the platform's real concurrency ceiling, not an assumed one.

nodes.title: Choose where accumulating state lives
nodes.text: Decide where the running model state is persisted between invocations, since Workers themselves are stateless and short-lived: Durable Objects, KV, R2, or an external database.
nodes.duration_basis: A consequential choice with a real consistency/latency trade-off; same calendar risk as other decision tasks.
nodes.exit_criteria: One state store chosen with its consistency guarantee stated.
nodes.risk_reason: A consequential choice (Durable Objects give strong consistency but add latency; KV/R2 are eventually consistent and cheaper) the plan can't make alone.

nodes.title: Confirm the model supports incremental updates
nodes.text: Confirm the chosen model type can actually be updated incrementally from a stream of deltas, since a full retrain on every delta will not fit the time or memory budget.
nodes.duration_basis: If no online variant is documented for the chosen algorithm, this stops being a lookup and becomes its own small research task.
nodes.exit_criteria: Confirmed online/incremental variant exists for the chosen algorithm, or an alternative chosen.
nodes.risk_reason: Some anomaly-detection methods have well-known online variants, others don't -- unknowable until the algorithm is picked.

nodes.title: Build state accumulation and reload
nodes.text: Build the accumulate/persist/reload cycle for the running model state across many independent, short-lived invocations.
nodes.duration_basis: Concurrent-writer correctness is the plan's one stated coverage gap (see sys-train's covers_why below); this is where it actually has to get solved in code, which is where estimates most often blow out.
nodes.exit_criteria: State survives across invocations and reflects every delta applied, under concurrent writers.
nodes.risk_reason: Where the open concurrency question below actually has to be resolved in code, not just decided on paper.

nodes.title: Handle worker failure
nodes.text: Design for a worker dying mid-chunk or a delta going missing: retries, idempotent shard ids, at-least-once delivery with dedupe in the reduce step.
nodes.duration_basis: Absent from the original pitch, so there's no prior design to build against -- real risk of discovering a second failure mode mid-implementation.
nodes.exit_criteria: A killed worker's chunk gets retried and its delta (if any) is neither lost nor double-counted.
nodes.risk_reason: Absent from the pitch as given; a distributed system that assumes every worker finishes is not a real distributed system.

nodes.title: Add per-pass observability
nodes.text: Emit per-pass metrics: shards completed, deltas emitted, bytes moved, invocation time, kill rate.
nodes.duration_basis: Mostly wiring against metrics that already exist elsewhere in the build; modest tail.
nodes.exit_criteria: A dashboard or log stream showing all five metrics for a real pass.
nodes.risk_reason: Without this, ops-e2e and ops-costmodel have nothing real to measure against.

nodes.title: Build a real cost projection
nodes.text: Project cost per full pass and per day at target scale -- invocations, GB moved, Durable Object time -- against a budget the pitcher has to supply.
nodes.duration_basis: Depends on three upstream measurements; if any came in worse than assumed, the cost model has to be redone before it's a stated figure.
nodes.exit_criteria: A dollar figure per pass and per day, checked against a stated budget.
nodes.risk_reason: Nowhere in the original pitch is there a cost figure at all; this is the fix.

nodes.title: Run end-to-end at target scale
nodes.text: Run the full pipeline on the full dataset at the target worker count, from a cold start.
nodes.duration_basis: The first point every prior piece has to actually work together, not just in isolation -- classic integration-day risk, where the pessimistic case is one full extra debugging pass.
nodes.exit_criteria: One complete pass at target scale, cold start to finished delta set, with no unhandled failures.
nodes.risk_reason: The first point every prior piece has to actually work together, not just in isolation.

nodes.title: Deploy and launch
nodes.text: Deploy path, rollback plan, secrets and limits configuration, a runbook, and a go/no-go checklist.
nodes.duration_basis: The launch gate itself; pessimistic case is a rollback dry run or secrets/limits review turning up something that has to be fixed before go-live.
nodes.exit_criteria: A deployed, rollback-capable system with a runbook a second engineer could follow.
nodes.risk_reason: The launch gate itself; blocked on everything else landing.
